cards.title: A microscopic lightning rod allowed humans to image individual atoms
cards.body: In 1981, IBM researchers Gerd Binnig and Heinrich Rohrer created the scanning tunneling microscope, unlocking the world of nanotechnology. The device sweeps a needle sharpened to a single atom just fractions of a nanometer above a surface. By exploiting quantum tunneling, where electrons leap across the empty gap, the microscope measures fluctuations in electrical current to trace the contours of individual atoms—rendering atomic surfaces visible for the first time.

cards.title: The creator of the GIF format insisted it is pronounced with a soft 'G'
cards.body: In 1987, Steve Wilhite and his team at CompuServe designed the Graphics Interchange Format, or GIF, to transfer color images across sluggish dial-up connections using LZW compression. While internet users have fought an endless war over whether to pronounce the acronym with a hard or soft consonant, Wilhite settled it definitively: it is pronounced 'jif.' The naming deliberately parodied the famous American peanut butter advertising slogan: 'Choosy developers choose GIF.'

cards.title: Thomas Edison did not invent the light bulb—he made it practical
cards.body: Electric lighting was not invented by Thomas Edison. Over twenty inventors, including Humphry Davy and Joseph Swan, demonstrated glowing filaments decades earlier, but their prototypes burned out within minutes or drew unsustainable amounts of current. Edison's actual triumph in 1879 was engineering a high-resistance carbonized bamboo filament operating in a high vacuum. His design drew little current and burned for over 1,200 continuous hours, transforming experimental curiosities into a practical commercial system.

cards.title: The zipper took twenty years and two inventors to stop popping open
cards.body: In 1893, American inventor Whitcomb Judson patented the 'clasp locker' as a fast alternative to lacing tall boots. However, his clunky hook-and-eye system jammed constantly and popped open unexpectedly. The breakthrough came two decades later when Swedish-American electrical engineer Gideon Sundback redesigned the mechanism in 1913. By replacing hooks with dozens of tiny interlocking metal teeth nestled along two fabric tapes, Sundback created the smooth, reliable fastener we use today.

cards.title: An accidental glow through black cardboard revealed the skeleton
cards.body: In 1895, German physicist Wilhelm Röntgen was investigating electrical discharges inside an evacuated Crookes glass tube in a dark room. Though he had carefully wrapped the tube in heavy black cardboard to block all visible light, a fluorescent barium-coated paper screen several feet away began mysteriously glowing. Realizing an unknown invisible radiation was escaping the glass, Röntgen investigated for weeks and produced the world's first X-ray image: the skeletal bones of his wife's hand.

quizzes.question: What quantum phenomenon allows the scanning tunneling microscope to map individual atoms?
quizzes.explanation: Quantum tunneling allows electrons to leap across a sub-nanometer vacuum gap between the probe tip and sample, creating a measurable current.

quizzes.question: What commercial brand inspired the intended pronunciation of the GIF format?
quizzes.explanation: Steve Wilhite and his CompuServe team pronounced it 'jif,' spoofing the slogan 'Choosy mothers choose Jif.'

quizzes.question: What organic material did Thomas Edison use in 1880 to create a 1,200-hour light bulb filament?
quizzes.explanation: After testing thousands of materials, Edison's team found that carbonized bamboo fibers could burn for over 1,200 continuous hours.

quizzes.question: Who redesigned earlier clumsy fasteners into the modern interlocking-teeth zipper in 1913?
quizzes.explanation: Gideon Sundback replaced clumsy hooks and eyes with interlocking metal teeth, creating the reliable modern zipper.

quizzes.question: What subject was captured in Wilhelm Röntgen's famous first X-ray photograph in 1895?
options: The bones of his wife's hand
A metal weight inside a wooden box
A coin inside a leather pouch
quizzes.explanation: Röntgen produced the first medical X-ray showing the skeletal bones and ring on his wife Anna Bertha's hand.

guesses.prompt: In what year was the GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) image standard released by CompuServe?
guesses.explanation: CompuServe released the GIF format in 1987 to compress 256-color images for slow dial-up modems.

guesses.prompt: For how many continuous hours could Thomas Edison's 1880 carbonized bamboo filament light bulb burn?
guesses.explanation: Edison tested thousands of plant fibers before finding that carbonized Japanese bamboo lasted over 1,200 hours.

misconceptions.claim: The creator of the GIF file format intended the acronym to be pronounced with a hard 'G'.
misconceptions.explanation: Steve Wilhite and the CompuServe development team specifically declared the pronunciation is 'jif' with a soft G, spoofing Jif peanut butter.

misconceptions.claim: Thomas Edison invented the world's first incandescent light bulb.
misconceptions.explanation: More than twenty inventors built incandescent bulbs before Edison; his real achievement was a practical, long-lasting carbonized filament that made commercial electric grids viable.
